questions.question: Lord William Bentinck with the support of Raja Rammohan Roy abolished the practice of ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sati**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sati:-**

 
 
• It is the name of an ancient Indian practice where women would die in the pyre of her dead husband.
 
• The practice was voluntary but most of the time, it was involuntary.
 
• If a woman had no surviving children who could support her, she was pressured to accept sati.
 
• Lord William Bentinck with the support of Raja Rammohan Roy abolished the practice of Sati.
 
• Bentinck passed the Bengal Sati Regulation, 1829.
 
 
• He issued Regulation XVII declaring Sati to be illegal and punishable in criminal courts.
 
• The ban was met by uproar because many people supported Sati at the time.
 
• The matter went to the Privy Council in London.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Polyandry**:-

 
 
• It is a form of polygamy in which a woman takes two or more husbands at the same time.
 
• It is contrasted with polygyny, involving one male and two or more females.
 
• Polyandry is a rare form of marriage, but it is practiced in some parts of the world, including the Tibetan Plateau, Nepal, and the Marquesas Islands.

questions.question: Who was the Viceroy of India when the Indian Arms Act, 1878, was passed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord Lytton**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lord Lytton:**

 
 
• Lord Lytton served as the Viceroy of India from 1876 to 1880.
 
• He was responsible for enacting the Indian Arms Act of 1878, which restricted Indians from possessing firearms.
 
• This act was highly controversial and seen as discriminatory, fueling anti-British sentiment.
 
• His administration was also marked by the disastrous handling of the Great Famine of 1876-1878.
 
• He was also the viceroy during the second Anglo-Afghan war.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lord Curzon:**

 
 
• Lord Curzon served as the Viceroy of India from 1899 to 1905.
 
• He is known for his policies of centralization and efficiency, but also for his divisive actions, such as the partition of Bengal in 1905.
 
• He implemented reforms in education, agriculture, and archaeology.
 
• He was known for his interest in preserving ancient monuments.
 
• His rule was a time of increased nationalism.
 
 
 
• **Lord Ripon:**
 
 
• Lord Ripon served as the Viceroy of India from 1880 to 1884.
 
• He is remembered for his liberal policies, including the repeal of the Vernacular Press Act and the introduction of local self-government.
 
• He attempted to pass the Ilbert Bill, which aimed to remove racial jurisdiction disparities in the courts.
 
• His rule is often viewed as a time of progressive reform.
 
• He is considered one of the most popular viceroys.
 
 
 
• **Lord Dufferin:**
 
 
• Lord Dufferin served as the Viceroy of India from 1884 to 1888.
 
• His tenure saw the annexation of Upper Burma in 1885.
 
• The Indian National Congress was founded during his viceroyalty in 1885.
 
• His rule was a time of increased British expansion.
 
• His rule was a time of increased political organization by Indians.

questions.question: Who became the first Governor–General of Bengal in 1773?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Warren Hastings__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The first governor-general in India (of Bengal) was Warren Hastings in 1773.
 
• He started his career as a writer (clerk) in the East India Company at Calcutta in 1750.
 
• Established revenue board in 1772.
 
• He Abolished the dual system of governance.
 
• He founded the Asiatic Society of Bengal with William Jones in 1784 in Calcutta.
 
• Warren Hastings laid the foundation of civil service and Lord Cornwallis reformed, modernized, and rationalized it.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9074044cf96dc1d09ca89eac99180c3d7440ade1b364d09d47931959bf693cc8.png] **Confusion Points__** 

__
 
• William Bentinck:

 
 
• Lord William Bentinck was the last Governor-General of Bengal and the first Governor-General of India.
 
• **The Charter Act of 1833 **made the Governor-General of Bengal the Governor-General of India.
 
• Lord William Bentinck is credited for the abolition of the system of ‘Sati’.
 
• The Governor-General of India laid the foundation for Calcutta Medical College. It was established in the year 1835.
 
• It was the first medical college in Asia.
 
• In 1835 Sir Charles Metcalfe succeeded Lord William Bentinck.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Robert Clive:

 
 
• Major-General Robert Clive was the first British Governor of the Bengal Presidency.
 
• Clive began as a writer for the East India Company (EIC) which established the military and political supremacy of the EIC by securing a decisive victory at the Battle of Plassey(1757) in Bengal.
 
• Robert Clive was the Governor of Bengal from 1757-60 and from 1765-67.
 
• Robert Clive started a ‘Society of Trade’ in 1765 but it was later abolished.
 
• Robert Clive Introduce Dual System where the company was the Diwan and the Nawab held the Nizamat.
 
 
 
• **Thomas Munro:**
 
 
• ​Major general Sir Thomas Munro was a Scottish soldier who was appointed the governor of Madras in 1820.
 
• He served till his death from cholera in 1827.
 
• He also served as an army officer in the East India Company.
 
 
 
• **Charles Cornwallis:**
 
 
• Charles Cornwallis was the governor-general of Bengal when the permanent settlement was introduced in **1793**. 
 
• In this system, the zamindars became the owners of the land and were required to pay a fixed amount to Britishers as tax every month.

questions.question: Who was the Governor - General of India when Doctrine of Lapse was introduced in India?

• The doctrine allowed the **British East India Company** to **take over the territories **of Indian rulers who died without a** male heir.**
 
• Lord Dalhousie implemented this policy in order to** expand British control **over India and to **eliminate **the local rulers who were seen as **obstacles to British rule.**
 
• The Doctrine of Lapse was highly **controversial** and led to widespread **resentment **among Indian rulers and their subjects.
 
• **Lord Mountbatten** was the **last British Governor-General of India,** who oversaw the transfer of power to India in **1947**.
 
• **Lord Cornwallis** was the **Governor-General of Bengal ,** who served from **1786 to 1793.**
 
• **Lord Canning** was the Governor-General of India during the **Indian Rebellion of 1857.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lord Mountbatten **was appointed as the** Governor-General of India in 1947**, and he played a key role in the **transfer of power** from the **British to the Indian government.**
 
• **Lord Cornwallis** was a **British military commander** who served as the Governor-General of India during a period of significant **British expansion** in India. 
 
 
• He is also known for his role in the** American War of Independence.**
 
 
 
• **Lord Canning** was the Governor-General of India during the Indian Rebellion of **1857**, which was a major uprising against British rule in India. 
 
 
• He is remembered for his efforts to **restore peace and order **in the aftermath of the rebellion.

questions.question: Who among the following Governor-Generals declared 'Sati' practice as illegal?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord William Bentinck**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Lord William Bentinck, the Governor-General of India from 1828 to 1835, declared the practice of **Sati illegal and punishable by law** in 1829.
 
• The regulation abolishing Sati was officially titled **Regulation XVII** and was passed on December 4, 1829.
 
• Bentinck's decision was influenced by strong opposition to Sati from reformers like **Raja Ram Mohan Roy**, who advocated for women's rights and called Sati a barbaric practice.
 
• The abolition applied to the territories under the control of the East India Company, including Bengal, Madras, and Bombay presidencies.
 
• The regulation classified Sati as culpable homicide, thereby making those involved in enforcing or facilitating the practice legally accountable.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sati Practice:**

 
 
• Sati was a funeral practice in which a widow immolated herself on her husband's funeral pyre.
 
• It was prevalent in certain parts of India and was often enforced due to social and religious pressures.
 
 
 
• **Raja Ram Mohan Roy's Role:**
 
 
• Raja Ram Mohan Roy, a prominent social reformer, campaigned extensively against Sati.
 
• He highlighted the inhuman nature of the practice and used religious texts to argue against its legitimacy.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Ban:**
 
 
• The abolition of Sati was a significant step in the direction of women's rights and social reform in India.
 
• It marked the beginning of a series of reforms aimed at curbing oppressive practices against women.
 
 
 
• **Legacy of Lord William Bentinck:**
 
 
• Bentinck is remembered as a reformist Governor-General who introduced several progressive policies, including the abolition of Sati and efforts to suppress Thuggee.
 
• His tenure laid the foundation for modern social reforms in colonial India.

questions.question: In 1836, ________ became the Governor General of India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Earl of Auckland**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **George Eden, 1st Earl of Auckland**, served as the Governor-General of India from 1836 to 1842.
 
• He is most known for his involvement in the **First Anglo-Afghan War (1839-1842)**, which ultimately ended in disaster for the British.
 
• Earl of Auckland succeeded Lord William Bentinck as the Governor-General.
 
• During his tenure, he implemented several administrative reforms and efforts to improve education and public works.
 
• He was eventually succeeded by Lord Ellenborough in 1842 following the failure in Afghanistan.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **First Anglo-Afghan War**

 
 
• The war was fought between the British East India Company and the Emirate of Afghanistan from 1839 to 1842.
 
• The conflict was initiated by the British to install a puppet regime in Afghanistan and counter Russian influence in the region.
 
• The war ended in a catastrophic retreat for the British, famously known as the Retreat from Kabul in 1842.
 
• It resulted in significant loss of life and resources for the British forces.
 
 
 
• **Administrative Reforms**
 
 
• Earl of Auckland focused on improving the administrative efficiency of the British Indian government.
 
• He supported the expansion of the educational system in India, including the establishment of schools and colleges.
 
• His tenure also saw the improvement of public works, such as the construction of roads and irrigation projects.
 
 
 
• **Legacy**
 
 
• Despite the failure in Afghanistan, Earl of Auckland's efforts in education and public works left a lasting impact.
 
• His tenure is often remembered for its administrative and infrastructural improvements in British India.
 
• He was later commemorated in various namesakes, including the Auckland Islands in the Southern Ocean.

questions.question: The Permanent Settlement introduced by Cornwallis was NOT prevalent in which of the following regions of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Punjab**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Permanent Settlement** was introduced by **Lord Cornwallis** in **1793**.
 
• It was also known as the **Zamindari System**.
 
• The system was implemented primarily in the regions of **Bengal**, **Bihar**, and **Odisha**.
 
• Under this system, the **zamindars** were recognized as the landowners and were responsible for collecting and paying land revenue to the British government.
 
• The system aimed to create a loyal class of landlords who would support British rule.
 
• The system was not implemented in the **Punjab** region, where different land revenue systems, like the **Mahalwari system**, were in place.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Bengal**__

 __
 
• **Bengal** was one of the first regions where the Permanent Settlement was introduced.
 
• The region was a significant revenue source for the British East India Company.
 
 
 
• **Bihar**__
 __
 
• **Bihar** also saw the implementation of the Permanent Settlement.
 
• The system had lasting effects on the agrarian structure and rural society of the region.
 
 
 
• **Odisha**__
 
 
• The Permanent Settlement was extended to **Odisha** as well.
 
• It influenced the economic and social dynamics of the region.

questions.question: Who among the following was the viceroy of India at the time of India’s independence from colonial rule on 15 August 1947?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord Mountbatten**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lord Mountbatten** was the last viceroy of India.
 
• He oversaw the transition of British India to independence, which occurred on **15 August 1947**.
 
• Lord Mountbatten was appointed as Viceroy in March 1947 and served until India gained independence.
 
• He played a pivotal role in the partition of India and Pakistan.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Lord Mountbatten's full name was **Louis Francis Albert Victor Nicholas Mountbatten**.
 
• He was a member of the British royal family and a close relative of Queen Elizabeth II.
 
• After India's independence, he served as the first Governor-General of independent India until June 1948.
 
• He was also involved in various other significant roles and responsibilities within the British Navy and government.
